21: - **Added a built-in interception rule for deletion endpoint paths**: Previously, the built-in destructive HTTP rule recognized only the DELETE **method**, but many applications allow deletion through GET/POST: calls such as `curl 'http://t/api/user/delete?id=1'` can delete real target data. An additional `deny` rule now covers `/delete /del /remove /unlink /erase /destroy` (the verb must be followed by a separator, so `/delivery`, `/details`, and `/delta` are not falsely blocked). Existing instances receive it on upgrade; it can be disabled or deleted under System → Command Interception.
22: - **Model fallback approval now has separate token usage statistics**: Approval calls previously had no independent accounting, leaving their cost unclear. They are now metered separately. A usage card below the Model Fallback Approval switch under System → Command Interception shows cumulative calls, input, output, cache reads and cache writes, plus a miniature daily usage chart for the last 30 days.
28: - **Push vulnerability discoveries to IM**: The new System → Notifications page can send scan discoveries through six channel types: **DingTalk, Feishu, WeCom, generic Webhook, Telegram, and email**. Each type supports any number of instances, with independent enablement, rate limits and filters.
29: - **Real-time and digest delivery modes**: Real-time mode sends each matching discovery immediately; digest mode combines discoveries into one message at a global interval (30 minutes by default), with new-discovery counts and severity distribution at the top. Configure two channels for high-severity real-time alerts and digests for everything else.
30: - **Four filtering dimensions**: Minimum severity, task/asset scope, vulnerability-type keyword inclusion and exclusion (exclusion takes precedence), and whether to receive disposition-status changes (off by default). Messages include a View Details button whose destination uses the global backlink address; leaving it empty omits the button.
31: - **Delivery history and manual resend**: Lists each delivery's status, attempt count, failure reason and channel, with channel/status filters. Failed entries can be resent with one click, resetting their retry count.
32: - **Masked channel credentials**: Webhook URLs, signing secrets, Bot Tokens and SMTP passwords are returned only as masks with a trailing-character hint. Returning the mask unchanged means no change; clearing the input deletes the field.
36: > This section records a security audit after the initial implementation. Each issue was reproduced, fixed, and covered by a regression test.
38: - **Fixed bypassing masks by changing destinations while retaining credentials (critical)**: Configuration merging preserved database values for all omitted keys. Changing only the destination while omitting credentials could therefore silently send stored credentials to an arbitrary address. A destination change now requires an explicit choice for every credential field: provide a new value or explicitly leave it empty if no longer needed.
39: - **Fixed missing escaping of untrusted content in Markdown-based channels**: Vulnerability titles and summaries come from model output, and asset URLs from scan results. Crafted titles could render clickable external links in DingTalk, WeCom or Feishu, while image syntax could trigger client requests and reveal readers' IP addresses. Content is now flattened to one line and Markdown metacharacters escaped at each channel's rendering boundary, rather than in the shared title function.
40: - **Fixed SSRF exposure through delivery destinations**: Loopback, private-network and cloud metadata addresses were previously all reachable; the first 200 bytes of failure response bodies entered `last_error` and appeared in delivery history, creating a semi-blind read primitive. Protection now operates at the **dial stage**, covers DNS rebinding, and rejects cross-host redirects. Loopback and link-local destinations require explicit `ARTEX_NOTIFY_ALLOW_LOCAL=1`; RFC1918 private networks remain allowed because private SMTP relays are common.
41: - **Fixed notification credentials leaking through errors**: DingTalk's `access_token`, WeCom's `key` and Telegram's bot token appear in URLs. On delivery failure, complete URLs reached `last_error`, delivery history, server logs and frontend notices. Errors are now redacted consistently, retaining only `scheme://host` and the underlying cause.
42: - **Fixed silent loss when truncated digests marked the entire batch delivered**: Omitted vulnerabilities appeared neither in the message nor in the failure list, while history reported success. Digests now pack **whole entries**, mark only included entries delivered, and requeue the rest for the next message without consuming retries. The header also states how many entries remain.
43: - **Fixed misspelled minimum severity silently disabling filters**: A typo such as `hgih` in `min_severity` assigned the unknown level ordinal 0, making the predicate always true. Users expecting only high-severity alerts instead received every vulnerability. The write path now validates the value and lists valid choices.
44: - **Fixed unreachable `rate_per_min = 0` (unlimited)**: The database write layer silently replaced explicit 0 with the default, leaving rate limiting active when operators expected it disabled. Defaults now apply at the API layer only when the field is absent.
45: - **Fixed digest channels bypassing the token bucket entirely**: `rate_per_min` previously had no effect in digest mode. The number of claimed entries is now bounded by both the current allowance and an in-memory limit.
46: - **Fixed batch-wide failure decisions using the largest attempt count**: An old delivery with two retries could force brand-new deliveries in the same batch into failed status, permanently losing new alerts before they received any retry. Decisions are now per delivery.
47: - **Fixed unparseable snapshots in digest batches being silently marked successful**: Rendering skipped these entries but the whole batch was still counted successful. They now fail explicitly with a reason.
48: - **Fixed per-channel delivery batches potentially outlasting their leases**: In multi-instance deployments, expired rows could be reclaimed, sent twice and have attempts incremented twice. The per-round limit is now derived from lease duration divided by single-delivery timeout, with assertions pinning the relationships among these constants.
49: - **Fixed Telegram truncation splitting HTML entities**: Truncation avoided partial tags but not entity fragments such as `&amp`, which could cause the parser to reject the **entire** message. It now avoids both.
50: - **Fixed email channels treating temporary SMTP failures as permanent**: 4xx replies such as greylisting `450` are temporary refusals and should be retried, but were previously terminal, causing every alert on greylisting servers to fail on its first attempt. The first response-code digit now distinguishes retryable 4xx from permanent 5xx failures.
51: - **Fixed nested submissions storing mask literals in the database**: Object fields such as `webhook.headers` must be masked or submitted as a whole. A mask sentinel nested inside an object was stored as a real value, silently breaking authentication. Such submissions are now explicitly rejected.
55: - **Vulnerability writes perform only one blind INSERT in the transaction**: `notification_events` and vulnerabilities are written in the same transaction, ensuring atomic consistency on commit. This INSERT deliberately does not read channel tables or run user filters, and is wrapped in `SAVEPOINT`; otherwise a misconfigured filter could abort the transaction and prevent a high-severity vulnerability from being stored.
56: - **Deliveries use leased claims rather than long transactions**: After claiming with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, rows become `sending` and `next_attempt_at` moves into the future as a lease. No database locks are held during delivery. Rows left by a crashed process are reclaimed after lease expiry, recovering automatically without unlimited retries.
57: - **Rate limiting does not consume retry budgets**: Compute the current allowance from the token bucket before claiming that many entries. Reversing the order would count rate-limited deliveries as attempted, exhausting the three-attempt budget through waiting alone.
63: - **Fixed permanent test-asset leaks caused by cleanup order in company ICP ownership tests**: `defer d.Close()` ran on function return before `t.Cleanup`, so cleanup statements used a closed connection and discarded their errors. Test companies and assets remained permanently and could break unrelated asset-count assertions. Connection closing now also uses `t.Cleanup`, registered first, and cleanup errors are surfaced.
69: - **Traffic lists now support content search, path/status/length filters and column sorting**: Filter by **response content** (full-text index), **path**, **status code** (exact or buckets such as `2xx`), and **response-length range**. Headers sort by time, status or response length, with preferences stored locally. Two new indexes apply automatically on upgrade; the Agent tool query contract is unchanged.
70: - **Added Clear All to traffic lists**: Deletes all traffic records regardless of filters and removes historical host directories no longer tracked by the index. It then runs full compaction and reports the actual space released. Traffic evidence attached to vulnerabilities is stored separately and is unaffected.
74: - **Fixed deleting traffic not releasing disk space**: Index databases were created without `auto_vacuum`, so files never shrank. The full-text index used `contentless_delete`, where `DELETE` wrote tombstones without reclaiming original postings; deletion actually enlarged indexes (a measured 6MB body produced a 16MB index that remained 16MB after deletion). New index databases enable `auto_vacuum=incremental`, and each deletion schedules chunked full-text merging and incremental reclamation in the background, gradually returning space to the system (104KB in the same scenario). Write locks are released between chunks to avoid blocking recording.
76: > Upgrade note: `auto_vacuum` can only be set when creating a database, so **existing instances retain the old index mode**. Incremental reclamation is a no-op there, with a startup log notice. Upgrading stops tombstone growth; use Clear All once to reclaim existing space and convert the database to incremental mode. Subsequent routine deletions then reclaim space automatically.
82: - **Fixed custom session headers not applying to one-shot LLM calls**: Goal decomposition (round 0) and cold-node compaction are one-shot calls without a transcript store or session ID in context, so gateways could not read the header. Endpoints such as opencode zen that return 400 without it failed in round 0 while later planner rounds worked normally. Both paths now explicitly attach an exploration-stable session ID, also attributing token usage to the correct exploration instead of losing it entirely.
88: - **Fixed MCP and custom-tool truncation failing and flooding context with large results**: MCP outputs previously bypassed truncation, while HTTP custom tools received an empty tool context and used a hard-coded 6000-character cap rather than the session setting. Both now use `actool.Capture`, truncating to session `MaxOutputChars` (30000 by default). With `ToolOutputDir` configured, full output spills to disk and messages retain only a leading excerpt and file pointer.
89: - **Upgraded norma to v0.4.3**: The harness applies `CaptureOnce` centrally, preventing any tool, including future additions, from overflowing context because truncation was not wired in.
95: - **Fixed activity streams failing behind reverse proxies**: SSE addresses previously always used `${hostname}:8787`. Pages loaded from `https://域名/` behind a proxy on 443 therefore targeted port 8787, which was not publicly exposed, causing repeated reconnections. Behavior now depends on `NODE_ENV`: production defaults to same-origin, while only `next dev` retains `:8787` to bypass Next.js SSE buffering. The `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` override remains available. README now documents reverse-proxy deployment.
101: - **Fixed missing scrolling when the By Asset discovery list overflowed**: The outer card had only `max-height`, not a definite height, so the scroll viewport could not resolve its percentage height. Large lists overflowed or were clipped without scrolling. The height limit now applies directly to the asset tree's native scroll container and adapts to the window height.
107: - **Capped the connection pool**: `database/sql` defaults to unlimited application connections and opens another whenever none are idle, eventually reaching PostgreSQL's `max_connections` (100 by default) and receiving rejections. The pool is now capped at 32; excess queries wait for an idle connection, making the same load slower rather than erroneous. Lower this cap as well if `max_connections` has been reduced.
108: - **Improved connection reuse**: `MaxIdleConns` defaults to 2, so connections beyond two concurrent requests were closed after use, requiring fresh TCP and PostgreSQL authentication handshakes next time. The idle cap now matches the total cap, with a 30-minute connection lifetime and 5-minute idle expiry to replace long-lived bad connections naturally.
120: - **Added a Vulnerabilities column to task lists**: Shows critical/high/medium/low counts, coloring nonzero buckets by severity so each task's vulnerability volume and distribution are visible at a glance.
124: - **Narrowed the Description / Goals columns**: Long text is ellipsized with full text on hover, reducing horizontal space consumed by lengthy content.
130: - **Simplified the planning overview (graph_overview) and capped its lists**: Recent facts, completed intents, pending intents, cold-area summaries and confirmed-vulnerability details now use a latest window plus total counts; omitted entries can be queried on demand. This substantially reduces per-round LLM context and long-task growth, including cold areas in related-task overviews.
134: - **Removed reversed duplicate edges between digest and finding nodes after folding cold nodes in the exploration graph**.
146: - **Added global asset interception rules (blocklist)**: Supports exact and fuzzy domain/IP/URL matches and CIDR ranges, with CRUD and enable/disable controls under System → Asset Interception. Built-in fuzzy rules block government (`.gov` / `.gov.cn`) and education (`.edu` / `.edu.cn`) sites by default.
147: - **Integrated asset interception into execution**: Before dispatching intents (`add_intent`) or inserting assets (`insert_assets`), the Agent checks target assets. Matching intents are not dispatched and matching assets are not inserted; asset information and the rejection reason are returned to the Agent.
148: - **Added task-level block/allow (allowlist) rules**: Independent of global rules and limited to the current task. Evaluation blocks first, then allows: any block match rejects; otherwise, when enabled task allow rules exist but none match, testing is disallowed. Without allow rules, the allowlist is inactive. Rules can be entered when creating tasks or managed in task-detail Overview.
149: - **Task templates now include preset categories and task-level block/allow rules**: Saved categories and rules populate the new-task form when applying a template.
155: - **Tightened the model judge output protocol to reduce truncation-related false allowances**: Reduced the verdict comment limit from 500 to 120 Chinese characters and required JSON only, without preambles or code blocks. This avoids `MaxTokens` truncation causing parse failures followed by fail-open handling.
161: - **Skip symbolic links during archiving instead of failing the entire archive**: The archive format supports only regular files and directories end to end. Previously any symlink in the work directory failed the whole task archive. Symlinks are now skipped and logged while other files are archived normally, without following links or escaping the directory tree.
167: - **Added a pre-login Usage Notice and Disclaimer dialog**: Agreement must be checked before login.
173: - **Adopted the AGPL-3.0 open-source license**, and completed the README license and disclaimer documentation.
186: - **Added an Exploration Feed to task details** (#144): A chronological timeline of exploration nodes (origin/goal/intent/fact/finding/hint/digest), with type filters, keyword search, ascending/descending order, pagination and auto-refresh. The first page in newest-first order is the live position and refreshes each round; elsewhere, only unread counts accumulate without disturbing reading, with an N new updates · Back to latest shortcut. Entries are grouped by day for orientation when paging through long tasks.
187: - **Each feed row displays its node ID** (#145), making it easier to cross-reference the exploration graph and locate nodes.
188: - **Expanded feed details show upstream/downstream nodes and anchored assets** (#147): Expanding an entry reveals its relationships; hovering a related entry shows a node card with type, status, source, time, summary and payload excerpt. Anchored assets appear with type labels and recognizable text. Data accompanies the feed page, so expansion makes no additional requests.
189: - **Feed search now supports node IDs** (#150): Alongside content/source matching, entering digits or the displayed #41 form locates the corresponding node exactly.
195: - **Intent deletion supports soft and hard deletion** (#149): Pending, running and paused intents can be deleted with a required reason; choose the mode in the confirmation dialog.
196: - **Soft deletion (default)**: Marks the intent deleted and stores the reason in a separate field, retaining the intent node and all its outputs and lineage.
197: - **Hard deletion**: Physically removes the intent and exclusive descendants supported only by it, cascading along output/intent chains to leaves to avoid orphaned data. Token accounting is rolled up under original dates; shared nodes referenced by other intents, goals and task-root facts are retained. The confirmation dialog shows the expected cascade node count.
199: Both modes notify the planner that the user deleted the intent, including the reason, so it can replan.
205: - **Approval records support status and decision-source filters** (#139), making target records easier to locate.
209: - **Pending approvals load independently of history pagination** (#133): They remain fully visible while browsing historical records.
215: - **Changed the Worker role description to general cybersecurity-platform wording** (#138).
219: - **Fixed cold-node compaction never triggering**: Connected the task planner to the Compactor, restoring previously unwired cold-digest execution.
225: - **Chat supports @ references to multiple record types and scrolling pagination** (#135): Reference candidates load additional pages while scrolling.
229: - **Constrained long message bubbles to the conversation panel** (#137), preventing overflow outside the conversation area.
230: - **Fixed uploads reporting Missing upload file before a new conversation existed**: Composer now snapshots `FileList` as an array before clearing the input and invoking the callback. Previously draft mode asynchronously created the conversation first; the live-bound `FileList` was empty when execution resumed, so the file field was missing and the backend returned 400.
236: - **Traffic recording proxies now listen only on 127.0.0.1 by default** (#129, #130), avoiding exposure of an open proxy on other interfaces.
242: - **Fixed the task-list page missing its global header in static exports**.
243: - **Completed associated-traffic mocks for demo vulnerability details, fixing a blank page**.
257: - **Approval records now link to their originating execution** (#125): Clicking Source opens the original complete conversation, paginates to the exact tool execution, expands its command/results and centers a highlight while keeping surrounding messages readable. Manual scrolling stops automatic adjustment. Ordinary chat, task Worker, planner and segmented main-Agent conversations are located through persisted `tool_use_id` and task mappings, with a new scoped call-ID index. Missing, duplicate or ambiguous associations produce explicit notices instead of jumping to another execution. Deleted conversations, archived tasks and missing records also receive clear notices.
262: - **Simplified model-review input** (#124, #125): The LLM judge used when no rule matches now receives versioned JSON containing only the current complete tool call, explicitly selected brief background and the local work directory. Background uses only genuine current user messages from chat/task main Agent; Workers omit intent summaries and clear inherited parent background. Planner and automatic sessions do not invent user messages. Task descriptions, goals, operation constraints, global exploration state, historical calls and complete Worker intents no longer enter operation review, but remain available to Agent execution and independent session auditing. Verdicts require JSON `decision`/`comment`, explaining the actual operation, consequences of success and matched rule; instructions in arguments or background cannot change review policy. The actual model input snapshot and fingerprint are saved. Older snapshots remain versioned rather than being reconstructed from current data.
266: - **Code-block-wrapped verdicts no longer silently allow execution** (#126): Previously, verdict JSON wrapped in ``` failed parsing and silently followed model-failure allowance. Code fences are now stripped before parsing; only a remaining parse failure uses the configured failure policy.
272: - **Added experimental noa context compaction** (norma upgraded to v0.4.0): Disabled by default and enabled in system settings. noa model-driven compaction replaces built-in compaction for main Agent, planner, Worker and chat. Original compacted text is archived centrally under `<workDir>/noa/<会话ID>/`, in globally unique session-ID directories rather than individual task directories. Integration failures fall back automatically without interrupting real tasks. The switch is read once per run and affects only subsequently started runs.
276: - **Exploration-graph tools reject calls without task context instead of panicking on nil**: Such calls now return explicit errors rather than dereferencing an empty store.
282: - **Supported legacy SSE MCP services** (#117): Compatible with servers offering only the older SSE transport.
288: - **Traffic searches match recorded hosts with port awareness** (#114): `traffic_search` includes ports in host matching to avoid mixing records from different ports on the same host.
289: - **A failed `traffic_search` description migration no longer stops later reporter migrations**: Individual migration failures are isolated.
295: - **Added separators between task vulnerability-retest options** (#122) for clearer visual grouping.
299: - **Fixed demo task details crashing entirely**: In mock mode, the Conversations tab requested `GET /api/tasks/<id>/side-questions` (side-question history), but no mock handler existed. The read fallback treated paths ending in s as collections and returned `[]`; `data.items` became `undefined`, and the side-question hook's `merge()` threw `TypeError: t is not iterable`. Because this occurred in the `setItems` updater, React rethrew it during render, beyond the caller's `catch`, and the error boundary displayed This page couldn't load. The mock now returns explicit empty side-question history, and `sideAPI.history` normalizes non-array `items` to `[]` as defense in depth.
312: - **Added DeepSeek's official web-search source**: Reuses the active LLM configuration. Unlike the other three sources, DeepSeek has no directly callable search API; search exists only as the `web_search_20250305` server tool in its Anthropic-compatible API and runs on DeepSeek's server. It therefore **requires the official DeepSeek endpoint and anthropic protocol**; OpenAI-protocol endpoints reject server tools. Each search **consumes an additional model call**, **bypasses the search outbound proxy**, and **is not captured in traffic records**. Results contain **titles and links only**, without summaries; WebFetch retrieves full text when needed. Settings explain these limitations but **do not enforce validation**; users can verify with Test Search.
318: - **Workers can review traces across work items**: Added `search_all_worker_traces` to search matching steps across every work item in the task without first knowing intent_id, and `get_worker_trace` to list a selected work item's steps, search them or retrieve complete content by step_id. This reuses observations not recorded as facts and avoids duplicate work.
319: - **Made `node_detail` available to workers**: Together with the trace-review tools, workers can directly retrieve full details using intent_id/node ID.
320: - **Explicitly announce planning rounds triggered by `add_hint`**: Previously hints were merely included in the overview for planners to notice. Now each call records one trigger announcing N human-added strategic hints, even for batches, explicitly identifying the round's cause and showing the hint contents.
324: - **Relaxed the global situation prompt**: Encourages divergent exploration and timely reporting of cross-intent leads rather than premature convergence.
325: - **Simplified worker boundary wording**: An initial obstacle is not proof of exhaustive exploration; finish reasonable bypass methods within the intent before concluding.
326: - Removed each asset's `related` parameter from `insert_assets`: It only decided whether to include an asset in the task scope and was never persisted. Re-registering the asset discarded it, and the UI could not show which assets had been deemed unrelated, leaving the model to make an extra judgment that could not be retained.
327: - **Test scope (`task_scope`) no longer depends on the asset-coverage switch**: Automatic `insert_assets` scope writes (`source='auto'`) now always run, and `add_task_scope` is always available to planner, task main Agent and goal-decomposition Agent. Scope defines authorization and asset-query filtering; coverage controls only whether it is used as a metric denominator. Previously disabling coverage broke both `auto`/`agent` write paths, leaving only manual UI entries in `task_scope`. `list_untested_assets` remains hidden when coverage is disabled because it is purely a coverage view.
331: - **Fixed assets leaking across tasks** (#59): `list_assets` hard-coded task ID 0 and queried the whole shared asset store, while models lacked a way to express scope filters. Assets from other tasks, especially IPs, were mistaken for current targets. Results now stay within `task_scope` for **this task and directly related tasks**, matching by **ownership**, not literal value: root domains include their subdomains/services/endpoints, and networks include contained hosts/services. Direct ID lookups also exclude out-of-scope assets. Non-task Auto/pentest contexts still fall back to the whole store. Also fixed the ownership gap where direct-IP hosts such as `http://1.2.3.4/api` failed network-scope matching. The UI Test Assets view, filtered by task producer, is unaffected.
332: - **Fixed worker cross-work review tools being unintentionally removed**: After adding `search_all_worker_traces` / `get_worker_trace` and `node_detail` to worker defaults, an older startup migration narrowing the tool surface unbound them again. They were removed from that list, with a one-time migration restoring bindings in previously migrated databases.
333: - **Fixed intermittent `/btw` side-question persistence failures**: Strip NUL (`�`) escapes unsupported by JSONB before storing side_question checkpoints.
339: - **Deduplicated task descriptions/goals in merged trigger sessions**: Multi-task merged triggers include each task's description/goals only once, preventing long goals from filling context repeatedly.
351: - Task main Agents support **multiple conversations**, with creation, switching and independent context resets; every conversation is interactive.
352: - Added persistent `/btw` **side questions**: Follow up without interrupting the main thread; Q&A survives restarts.
353: - Added `source_task_ids` to `spawn_task`, allowing new tasks to **inherit read-only** assets and findings from source tasks.
357: - Disabled workers' cross-engagement memory and narrowed their default tools: Reading context and cross-work review are planning duties; workers execute and write back a single intent.
358: - Simplified default worker prompts; removed `terminated` and `worker_name` from `get_worker_output`; simplified `insert_assets` / `list_assets` descriptions.
362: - Fixed work ending early after **idle turns**: Models sometimes spent an entire turn thinking, with neither body text nor tool calls. The harness saw a natural end (`end_turn` without `tool_use`) and returned `completed` with an empty summary, ending unfinished intents without any textual conclusion. None of the five LLM retry layers could intervene: this was not an error; same-provider safe-window retries require stream failure; circuit breakers treat `err == nil` as success; intent reruns require `model_error`; and SDK empty-response detection checks whether any event was yielded, including thinking deltas. The work Stop hook now detects these turns and injects a continuation instruction, preserving existing thinking for the next step. It deliberately avoids resending unchanged requests because these idle turns generally reflect stable prompt/context behavior, not random failures; resending would only repeat the thinking.
363: - Reused the LLM Retry and Backoff page's **empty-response retry count**: Both address completion without substantive output, using different detection and recovery methods. Default 2; `-1` disables continuation and restores the previous behavior. This is a **total per-intent** limit, not a consecutive-turn count: the harness allows only one push after consecutive idle turns and refreshes that allowance only after a real tool turn, so the setting bounds tool → idle → push → tool → idle loops that consume intent budgets. Triggers log `[work <worker> · #<意图>] 空转回合…注入续跑指令 (n/N)`. See `docs/LLM重试设计.md` §1.1.
364: - Fixed `/btw` context budgets and input layout in long conversations; use a fallback side-request ID generator in insecure non-HTTPS contexts.
370: - Vulnerabilities support **multiple associated traffic-evidence records**, with ordering, notes and roles (request/response/corroboration).
371: - Report Agents **automatically associate** relevant traffic evidence before writing reports.
372: - Added an Agent **traffic-binding switch** and completed evidence handoffs between Agents.
378: - Added **conversation-level vulnerability retesting**, running in an independent Agent conversation with status shown in lists and details.
384: - Approval records now include **details and execution audits**: View tool-request context, initial model/rule decisions, execution output and argument fingerprints.
396: - Fixed connection tests omitting custom session headers and causing opencode zen to return 400.
402: - MCP HTTP transport can **skip TLS certificate verification** for self-signed services.
408: - Conversation lists group by Agent, with expand/collapse and independent pinning; conversations can be filtered by Agent.
409: - Attack-chain graphs render digest nodes and collapse their members.
413: - Fixed blank pages caused by unsynchronized login credentials.
414: - Interception notices now explicitly identify platform controls, avoiding confusion with defenses on the target.
420: - Added **one-click updates from the page**: A Version and Updates card appears in system settings, and the top bar signals new releases. The process downloads a release package → verifies `SHA256SUMS` → smoke-tests → stages → exits for the supervisor script to restart and replace the application; the page refreshes automatically.
421: - Added supervisor scripts `start.sh` / `start.bat` as official startup entry points, included in release packages and Docker images (`install.sh` unchanged). They choose whether to restart by exit code and forward SIGTERM to artex. Verification and replacement remain in Go, keeping scripts simple.
422: - Automatic fallback on failure: Failed verification or smoke tests discard the update and keep the current version. Three consecutive startup failures roll back to the previous version. Settings also offer manual rollback; database schemas are not rolled back.
423: - Updates require GitHub domains and HTTPS; the release source is not configurable. Development builds disable one-click updates. GitHub results are cached for 30 minutes to prevent top-bar checks exhausting API quotas.
427: - Docker updates replace the application, not the image: Toolchains are not upgraded, and recreating a container restores its image's version. Use `docker compose pull artex` when needed.
428: - Release-package `skills/` are not synchronized, so newly added built-in skills do not take effect automatically.
429: - Updates restart the application and interrupt running tasks.
